item.title: Zelenskyy Says Open to Energy Ceasefire if Russia Agrees
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, says that the US joining Saudi Arabia in military attacks on the Houthis could deepen what he calls a “mini forever war” without producing a clear end state. Ellen Wald, president of Transversal Consulting and nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council Global Energy Center, says she sees no recent move by the president that could materially bring down oil prices. Republican Congressman Tim Moore of North Carolina said he believes Democrats are unlikely to win a House majority, but criticized their stated priorities if they do, arguing that investigations and efforts to impede opponents should not dominate Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Moore: Congress Should Focus on Economy, Not Investigations
item.description: Republican Congressman Tim Moore of North Carolina said he believes Democrats are unlikely to win a House majority, but criticized their stated priorities if they do, arguing that investigations and efforts to impede opponents should not dominate Congress. Speaking from a forklift manufacturing plant in his district, Moore pointed to the working families tax cut and job creation, and urged lawmakers to address economic challenges, including affordability, and help Americans who are struggling. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wald: Middle East Risks Keep Oil’s Risk Premium in Place
item.description: Ellen Wald, president of Transversal Consulting and nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council Global Energy Center, says she sees no recent move by the president that could materially bring down oil prices. She says short-lived dips driven by statements or social media have not lasted, and the market has largely shed expectations that the conflict will soon end. Wald says oil-market buffers built up over the prior six months are nearly exhausted, while reported oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz—including ship-to-ship transfers—may not be sustainable. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Miller Warns US-Saudi Strikes May Not Stop Houthis
item.description: Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, says that the US joining Saudi Arabia in military attacks on the Houthis could deepen what he calls a “mini forever war” without producing a clear end state. He notes that US forces previously conducted more than a thousand strikes on Houthi facilities, but argues airstrikes are unlikely to change the group’s political calculations. Miller says Saudi infrastructure is especially vulnerable because the Houthis have demonstrated the ability to strike airports and oil facilities. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Floats Potential Meeting With Kim Jong Un During Asia Trip
item.description: President Donald Trump said he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during an upcoming trip to Asia, stoking speculation about renewed US outreach to the reclusive regime.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Trump-Putin Diesel Deal
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Stocks fluctuated near all-time highs Monday as traders looked ahead to the start of the earnings season and inflation data that will be key in shaping the Federal Reserve outlook. With Corporate America navigating one of the strongest profit cycles in recent history, equities have also defied concerns about elevated energy costs and bond yields. President Trump’s deal with Moscow on its diesel exports and his praise for Vladimir Putin are just the latest in a string of Russia-related news that have sparked criticism from Republicans weeks ahead of a midterm election that increasingly favors Democrats.
On today's episode: Jeff Mason, Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Margie Patel, Allspring Global Investments Senior Portfolio Manager Veena Ali-Khan, Bloomberg News Reporter Tal Keinan, Sky Harbour CEO (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He’s Looking Into Guilfoyle Allegations, ‘Not Happy’
item.description: President Donald Trump said his administration was scrutinizing US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle following allegations of unethical conduct and reports that he was considering removing her from the post.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin Causes GOP Heartburn
item.description: President Trump’s deal with Moscow on its diesel exports and his praise for Vladimir Putin are just the latest in a string of Russia-related news that have sparked public criticisms from Republicans weeks ahead of a midterm election that increasingly favors Democrats. We get more from Jeff Mason, Bloomberg News White House Correspondent. Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence discusses the AI data center build-out reaching the $1.7 trillion mark. Needham's Laura Martin examines the path ahead for new media powerhouse Skydance. Plus - Tim Cahill, Lockheed Martin's President of Missiles & Fire Control, joins to discuss the defense company's new missile interceptor system. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Airport Carnage Pressures Trump to Boost US Role in Yemen
item.description: A barrage of drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia has intensified pressure on Washington to step up efforts to help its close ally battle Iran-backed Houthi militants in neighboring Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan and Veena Ali-Khan

item.title: Venezuela Sends Another Maduro-Linked Businessman to Face Charges in US
item.description: A Colombian businessman who operated for years in Venezuela is expected in US court to face criminal charges tied to more than $2 billion in government contracts in the South American nation.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch and Andreina Itriago

item.title: Saudi Arabia Fends Off More Attacks in Critical Moment for MBS
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is facing one of his most serious challenges since rising to power almost a decade ago as the kingdom grapples with the fallout from fatal attacks by Houthi militants.
item.dc:creator: Christine Burke

item.title: Tusk Says Germany Detains Two for Arson at Polish Starlink Base
item.description: German police detained two Turkish citizens suspected of setting fire to a Starlink station near Warsaw last month, Polish authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski

item.title: Trump's Diesel Dealwith Putin Threatens New Rift with Zelenskyy
item.description:
Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel supplies threatens to open a new rift between the US leader and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Anthony Halpin explains why the "energy ceasefire" declared by Trump may not be what it seems. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Must Pressure Russia, Not Ukraine, Says Poland's Sikorski
item.description: Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski says President Donald Trump should be putting more pressure on Russia and not Ukraine to end the war. He also says European sanctions against Vladimir Putin are the "toughest so far." He spoke with Bloomberg's Oliver Crook on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Says Iran’s IRGC Directed Incident at Airbase Used by US
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was “almost certainly” responsible for an alleged terror plot at a British airbase used by the US.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Wins Court Nod to Visit Father Before Vote
item.description: Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has authorized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to visit his father and former President Jair Bolsonaro who’s under house arrest less than two weeks before the presidential runoff.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Pulice

item.title: Burnham Fuels Dispute on Russia Brexit Role Before EU Summit
item.description: The UK government sought to play down Andy Burnham’s claim of Russian interference in the Brexit vote of 10 years ago, ahead of what is likely to be a fraught debate over the prime minister’s plan for closer ties with the European Union.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Chloe Chaplain
